body:
Public documentation findings for issue #976 (`assets/posts/heidenhain.cps` and `crates/app/tests/program_units.rs`):

| Point | Finding | Source | Confidence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Program start and end unit (`G70` / `G71`) | Confirmed. Write `G70` for inches in the opening `%` block and the closing `N99999999 %` block. Both blocks must use the same unit code. Standard motion and blank codes (`G00` to `G03`, `G30`, `G31`, `I`, `J`, `R`) stay unchanged. | HEIDENHAIN *TNC 640 ISO Programming* (`892909-25`), §1.3 (p. 39), §4.3 (pp. 130–131), [`892909-25.pdf`](https://content.heidenhain.de/doku/tnc_guide/pdf_files/TNC640/34059x-07/diniso/892909-25.pdf) | stated in the source |
| Path feed rate `F` unit in `G70` | Corrected. Do not write `F` in `inch/min`. The TNC 640 requires `F` in `1/10 inch/min` (`10 * mm_per_min / 25.4`). For example, `10 inch/min` requires `F100`, and `9.84 inch/min` requires `F98.4`. | HEIDENHAIN `892909-25`, §5.1 (p. 200): "in 1/10 inch/min in inch-programs, for resolution reasons"; HEIDENHAIN *Klartext Programming* (`892903`, `content.heidenhain.de`); EMCO WinNC TNC 640 (`emco-world.com`); Siemens NX CAM Community thread *Heidenhain TNC640 feed rate in inch units coming out 10x operation programmed feed rate* (`community.sw.siemens.com`) | stated in the source |
| Rapid feed `FMAX` | Confirmed. Write `FMAX` on a single block for rapid motion in `G70`. `FMAX` takes no unit scale factor. | HEIDENHAIN `892909-25`, §5.1 (p. 200); EMCO WinNC TNC 640 (`emco-world.com`) | stated in the source |
| Linear axes (`X`, `Y`, `Z`, `I`, `J`, `R`) and inch resolution | Confirmed. Under `G70`, coordinate and arc words use inches (`mm / 25.4`). Standard inch programming resolution is `0.0001` inch (4 decimal places). Coordinate fields list `-99999.9999` to `+99999.9999`, and max machine travel is `100 m` (`3937` inches). | HEIDENHAIN `892909-25` (`G70`); HEIDENHAIN `892905-25`, [`892905-25.pdf`](https://content.heidenhain.de/doku/tnc_guide/pdf_files/TNC640/34059x-07/zyklen/892905-25.pdf); Chudov TNC display reference (`chudov.com`) | stated in the source |
| Cycle length and depth parameters (`Q200` to `Q205`, `Q256`, `Q257`) | Confirmed. Cycle clearances, depths, and step lengths convert to inches (`mm / 25.4`) under `G70`. | HEIDENHAIN `892905-25`, §3.3 Cycle 200 (pp. 81–82), §3.8 Cycle 205 (pp. 95–98); HEIDENHAIN `892909-25` | stated in the source |
| Smoothing tolerance `G62 T` (`Cycle 32`) | Confirmed. Tolerance `T` uses the active length unit (`inch` under `G70`, so `smoothTol / 25.4`). | HEIDENHAIN `892905-25`, Cycle 32 `TOLERANCE (DIN/ISO: G62)` (§10.4 / §11.5, p. 275); HEIDENHAIN `892909-25` | stated in the source |
| Rigid tapping pitch `Q239` (`Cycle 207` / `G207`) unit and sign | Confirmed. `Q239` uses the active length unit per revolution (`inch/rev` under `G70`, so `pitch_mm / 25.4`). Sign `+` sets right-hand threads and `-` sets left-hand threads. | HEIDENHAIN `892905-25`, §4.3 Cycle 207 (pp. 111–116); HEIDENHAIN `892909-25` | stated in the source |
| Unit-invariant parameters (`S`, `Q210`, `Q211`, `Q208=FMAX`, mode flags, comments) | Confirmed. Spindle speed `S` (`rev/min`), dwells `Q210` and `Q211` (seconds), mode flags (`Q212`, `Q258`, `Q259`, `Q379`, `Q395`), `Q208=FMAX`, and semicolon comments do not depend on `G70` or `G71`. | HEIDENHAIN `892905-25`, §§3.3, 3.8, 4.2, 4.3; HEIDENHAIN `892909-25` | stated in the source |
| Cycle Q feed parameters (`Q206` in `G200`, `G205`, `G206`; `Q253` and numeric `Q208` in `G205`) | Manual `892905-25` prints only `mm/min` (`0` to `99999.999` or `99999.9999`) and omits inch feed rules. Earlier TNC MOD manuals (`TNC 410/426/430` §12.12, `iTNC 530` §17.11, `TNC 620` §16.7) state to "enter the feed rate larger by a factor of 10". No public TNC 640 `G70` cycle example explicitly confirms `Q206` or `Q253` in `1/10 inch/min`. | HEIDENHAIN `892905-25` (omits inch unit); HEIDENHAIN *TNC 410/426/430* (§12.12, p. 411) / *iTNC 530* (§17.11, p. 541) / *TNC 620* (§16.7, p. 481) | not found |
| Decimal digits and upper limit for `F` in `G70` (`1/10 inch/min`) | Manual `892909-25` (§5.1, p. 200) omits an upper limit and decimal count for `F` in `G70`. One real TNC 640 user report on Siemens NX Community shows `F98.4` (`1` decimal place) runs correctly, while `ff` in `heidenhain.cps` rounds to integers. | HEIDENHAIN `892909-25`, §5.1 (omits rule); Siemens NX CAM Community (`community.sw.siemens.com`) | not found |
| Inch numeric limits (`3937` in vs `99999.9999`, `Q256` min, 5-decimal `Q239`) | Manuals `892905-25` and `892909-25` print metric bounds only (`0` to `99999.9999`, `-99.9999` to `+99.9999`). They do not state if `Q256` accepts values smaller than `0.1` mm in inch mode or if 5-decimal TPI pitches (such as `1/32` = `0.03125` `inch/rev`) in `Q239` run at `0.0001` inch resolution. | HEIDENHAIN `892905-25` & `892909-25` (omitted) | not found |

## Not found

- **Numeric cycle Q feeds (`Q206`, `Q253`, numeric `Q208`) in TNC 640 inch programs:** Manual `892905-25` writes only `mm/min` in Cycle 200, Cycle 205, and Cycle 206, and does not include `1/10 inch/min`. General HEIDENHAIN feed rules (`892909-25` §5.1 and older TNC MOD sections) indicate that `1/10 inch/min` (`10 * inch/min`) applies to `Q206` and `Q253`, but no official TNC 640 `G70` cycle listing proves this directly. Note that `heidenhain.cps` writes `Q208=FMAX`, which needs no numeric feed value.
- **Decimal count and max bound for `F` in `G70`:** Manual `892909-25` does not state if `G70` `F` allows 1, 2, or 3 decimal places or requires whole numbers, and omits an inch max limit.
- **Inch limits for coordinates, `Q256`, and 5-decimal `Q239` pitches:** The manuals omit separate inch bounds (`3937` inch travel limit vs `99999.9999` numeric field), exact `Q256` inch minimum, and whether 5-decimal imperial thread pitches (for example 32 TPI = `0.03125` `inch/rev`) fail or round in `Q239`.

## Suggested changes (no code)

1. **`assets/posts/heidenhain.cps` — Post units and header/footer:** Change `programUnits` from `mm` to `mm inch`. Read `postOptions.Units` (`inch` or `mm`, default `mm`). Write `G70` instead of `G71` in the first `%<name> G70 *` block and last `N99999999 %<name> G70 *` block for inch programs.
2. **`assets/posts/heidenhain.cps` — Length, arc, tolerance, and Q-parameter scaling:** Divide all linear coordinates (`X`, `Y`, `Z`, `I`, `J`, `R`), smoothing tolerance (`G62 T`), cycle depths/clearances/steps (`Q200` to `Q205`, `Q256`, `Q257`), and rigid tapping pitch (`Q239`) by `25.4` in inch mode. Format linear coordinates (`fu`) to 4 decimal places (`0.0001` inch) instead of 3 decimal places. Scale `ARC_CHORD_TOL` (`0.001` mm) and the `Q256` chip-break retract limit (`Math.min(1, p.Q)`, now `1` mm) by `1 / 25.4` (or evaluate in `mm` before conversion). Convert or label `D` and `R` in `toolNote()` `;` comments so they match the document unit.
3. **`assets/posts/heidenhain.cps` — Feed rate `F` and cycle Q feeds (`Q206`, `Q253`):** Convert inch path feed `F` to `1/10 inch/min` (`10 * mm_per_min / 25.4`), not `inch/min`. Keep `FMAX` and `Q208=FMAX` unchanged. Compare `machine.feedRateMax` against the physical feed rate consistently before applying any `10x` control factor. Check on a real control if `Q206`, `Q253`, and floating-tap `Q206` resolution checks also take `1/10 inch/min` and if `F` in `G70` keeps 1 to 2 decimal places (instead of `Math.round`).
4. **`assets/posts/heidenhain.cps` — `Q239` inch check:** Check if 5-decimal imperial pitches (such as `0.03125` for 32 TPI) must be rounded to 4 decimal places (`0.0001` inch) or rejected by the rigid-tapping resolution check.
5. **`crates/app/tests/program_units.rs` — Inch test support:** Move `heidenhain` from `MM_ONLY` to `INCH_POSTS` with inch golden files and keep existing `mm` goldens byte-identical. Update `program_units.rs` for Heidenhain syntax because `same_program_in_inch()` checks `F` against `vx / 25.4` (`inch/min` instead of `1/10 inch/min`) and parses `<LETTER><FLOAT>` words instead of `Q<n>=+<float>` and `%<name> G70 *`.

A check on a real control is still needed before cutting. Test a posted `G70` program on a real TNC 640 control to confirm `Q206` and `Q253` feed units (`1/10 inch/min` vs `inch/min`), decimal `F` behavior, and `Q239` inch thread pitch behavior before you cut parts.
